body:
## Summary

Give each AI controller its own `boost::mt19937` stream, derived from the game seed and player number, and provide that stream to its implementation during initialization. Scope legacy synchronized random calls made during AI decisions to that controller's stream. Save and restore each stream in version 121 saves; older saves derive the stream from their saved game seed.

This prepares AI decisions for possible parallel execution. It does not run AI updates on multiple threads in this PR.

## Compatibility and game feel

- AI choices and therefore game trajectories, pacing, and difficulty can change. A maintainer playthrough is needed to assess the feel.
- Existing save formats remain loadable (`MINIMUM_VERSION_MINOR` stays 58); version 121 saves include the per-AI stream state.
- Replays from before version 121 and network clients before protocol 44 are rejected because they use different AI random behavior.
- This is a core behavior change and requires explicit approval from another human maintainer under `AGENTS.md` before merge.

## Validation

- macOS release build passed: `scons -Q -j8 release=1 server=0`.
- AI save portability harness passed.
- Team stats save harness, including replay and protocol acceptance gates, passed.
- Two 2,000-tick Cortex vs Nicowar games on `maps/balanced_for_2.map`, seed 123, produced 96 orders each, identical replay files and identical per-tick checksum sidecars; both ended with checksum `3a679efc`.
- Loading a version 121 initial save and running to tick 2,000 reproduced all per-tick team/entity telemetry records. Its aggregate checksum differs because `MapHeader::checkSum` includes `versionMinor`, which changes on save/load.
- An older save loaded and ran for 10 ticks.
- Cross-platform checksum equivalence has not yet been verified.

[Replay, checksum, and save evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/evidence-ai-random-streams/artifacts/ai-rng-pr)
title: Give each AI controller an independent random stream
